At 0% research progress, prioritize a reproducible extension of the supplied HSTU diagnostic adapter. No measured results currently establish which intervention improves validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, qualitative feedback favors specific recent purposes over broad historical associations. Measure recent-context dependence without equating sensitivity with intent. Second, single-negative margins describe local separation. They cannot establish top-10 competition. Third, left padding requires final-nonpadding readout. Removing the final item also changes that readout’s anchor.

**Insights from related work.** HSTU’s positional/temporal biases make deletion affect both evidence and attention geometry [1,6]. Verify implemented components before ablation. Sequence research separates order effects from catalog availability [2]. Sensitivity can also reflect fragility rather than useful sequence learning [8,9]. Sampled metrics can change model comparisons [3]. Keep the pinned benchmark as the selection criterion.

The framework has three directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-history dependence | Feedback; sequence research | Paired, anchor-preserving perturbations | Dependence does not identify intent |
| Ranking competition | Positive–negative margins | Fixed 99-negative target ranks | Sampled ranks do not establish catalog performance |
| Evidence sufficiency | Metadata; selective prediction [4] | Explicit unknown states | Missing specifications imply uncertainty |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Paired recent-history rank probe — 4/7/5.** Originality: + integrates HSTU geometry controls; − established perturbation methods. Potential: + guides focused experiments; − predictive validity remains untested. Difficulty: + reuses inference; − geometry-preserving masking requires architectural support [1–3,6].
2. **Representation-spectrum probe — 2/6/2.** Originality: + examines history features; − established effective rank. Potential: + separates directional and dimensional concentration; − negligible isotropic noise can appear high-rank. Difficulty: + bounded SVD; − variance and normalization require explicit definitions [5,7].
3. **Metadata evidence ledger — 4/6/5.** Originality: + separates unknown compatibility from conflict; − adapts selective prediction. Potential: + grounds feedback; − specifications may be absent. Difficulty: + deterministic extraction; − domain-specific rules need evidence checks [4].

Select **idea 1**: it directly addresses the feedback without fitting another predictor. Retain idea 2 as an inexpensive complementary measurement. Truncate histories once, preserve the final observed item in primary comparisons, and remove equal counts of recent versus oldest context without backfilling. Test anchor removal separately. Compare compacted deletion with position-preserving attention masking only where faithfully supported.

```text
fix users, checkpoint, windows, targets and candidates
score intact, suffix and matched-removal histories
read final nonpadding HSTU features
record paired ranks, hits and top-10 overlap
bootstrap paired users within each category
average category means equally
```

Training-prefix targets remain in-sample despite diagnostic holdout. Report them separately from authorized validation perturbations; leave host evaluation unchanged. Preserve diagnostic entry points, definitions, missingness and sample counts. Use one checkpoint/category, fixed seeds and trial-local artifacts. Report geometry, timestamp and readout limitations; claim neither causal intent nor improved generalization. Repeated validation tuning risks selection overfitting; diagnostic predictive validity remains exploratory.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware diagnostic adapter with fixed-candidate, paired recent-context perturbations of each category’s single trained HSTU, separating context removal, attention geometry, and changes to the final observed item.
idea.motivation: Qualitative feedback suggests that broad historical associations may outweigh specific recent purposes. Existing single-negative margins cannot characterize top-10 competition. Controlled perturbations can identify model dependence and motivate training hypotheses, while preserving the distinction between dependence, fragility, memorization, and causal user intent.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve view.model as the actual trained nn.Module and the host ModelView interfaces, including item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain existing valid probes, but leave unavailable metadata category breakdowns empty and return unavailable/null with reasons for empty valid samples rather than healthy-looking zeros. Do not infer unavailable ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores or simulator traits.

Use eval mode and torch.no_grad(), restoring the previous model mode in a finally block. Inspect only the supplied implementation when integrating the adapter: the available description does not establish whether timestamps, explicit position IDs or arbitrary attention masks are supported. Preserve log2feats(sequence) compatibility; any optional diagnostic path must delegate to the same trained module and weights. Do not assume that supplying zeros preserves positions: HSTU preprocessing may compact histories or regenerate positions. Geometry-preserving masking is available only if removed keys/values are excluded from attention, surviving position IDs and timestamps remain unchanged, the causal mask remains valid, and padding stays excluded. Zeroing embeddings alone is insufficient. Keep attention normalization policy fixed; removal can still change normalization through its valid-token set. If these controls cannot be implemented faithfully, report the arm as unavailable and describe compacted deletion as a joint evidence-and-geometry intervention. Do not disable temporal components that the supplied model does not implement.

Use seed 42 for diagnostics. Select at most 200 eligible training users per category by sorted user ID followed by a seeded permutation. Reserve the last training interaction as the diagnostic target, explicitly labeling all resulting measurements in-sample because fitting may already have used that target. Exclude the target from the diagnostic input prefix; earlier genuine occurrences may remain and must be flagged as repeat-target cases. Truncate that prefix once to the trained model's maximum history length before constructing any variants. Require at least three nonpadding interactions. Let n be this bounded length and k=min(5,floor((n-1)/2)); retain the final observed item as the common anchor. Define intact=history, suffix=history[-min(10,n):], remove_recent_context=history[:n-1-k]+history[-1:], remove_old_context=history[k:], and remove_anchor=history[:-1]. The two context-removal variants remove exactly k items and preserve the anchor. The suffix arm is descriptive and is not an equal-count control. Never backfill from outside the original bounded window. Report suffix cases that are identical to intact as unaffected. Keep surviving timestamps aligned with their items; preserve original timestamp values and any target/query-time convention rather than recomputing times from shortened histories.

For training diagnostics, draw 99 unique real-item negatives uniformly without replacement, excluding the target, padding, reserved tokens and every item in that user's training history. Use one shared sorted-user iteration and seeded generator per category and persist selected user IDs, windows and candidate IDs beneath the trial directory. Mark insufficient-catalog cases unavailable. Reuse identical candidates across variants and score through predict_score, adapting only tensor shapes according to the existing contract rather than assuming dot-product scoring. For left-padded sequences, read the greatest index with a nonzero item, never count-1. Preserve the documented host tie handling when supplied; otherwise use descending score and ascending item ID for diagnostic ties and disclose this rule. Define target rank as one plus its preceding-candidate count, hit as rank<=10, and top-10 overlap as intersection size divided by 10 on the same 100-item diagnostic candidate set. Define delta rank=perturbed rank−intact rank and delta HR=perturbed hit−intact hit. The anchor-removal arm changes the readout anchor and must be reported separately.

Authorized validation diagnostics must use the host-supplied validation users, targets and exact pinned candidate sets, without accessing hidden test data or changing host evaluation. Use all 200 validation users/category for intact diagnostic reproduction when available; report eligible subsets for perturbations separately, with intact-versus-perturbed changes computed on the same eligible users. If exact candidate sets or validation access are not exposed through the authorized interface, mark this diagnostic unavailable rather than reconstructing a purported host score. Training-prefix diagnostics and validation results must remain separate.

Record category, eligible/affected/unavailable user counts and reasons, original and retained lengths, timestamp spans where available, repeat-target status, per-user ranks/hits/overlaps and all perturbation settings. Timestamp spans use max(time)−min(time) in documented units; absent or unparseable timestamps yield unavailable spans. Prespecify 2,000 paired bootstrap replicates with seed 42, resampling the same user indices for all conditions within each category and equally averaging the four category means. Report 2.5th and 97.5th percentile intervals, conditional on the fitted models and fixed candidate sets. Do not impute a missing category as zero or publish a four-category macro estimate if a category has no eligible users. These intervals exclude training-seed variation, candidate-sampling variation and repeated-selection optimism. History-length and training-frequency strata are exploratory and must disclose group sizes; they must not drive an unreported search over thresholds.

For the optional representation probe, independently sample up to 2,048 real item embeddings and up to 200 final-nonpadding history features per category with seed 42. Report row norms, raw mean off-diagonal cosine over nonzero rows, centered total variance ||X_centered||_F^2/(N−1), centered and uncentered singular spectra, leading singular-energy share sigma_1^2/sum(sigma^2), and singular-value effective rank exp(−sum(p log p)), p=sigma/sum(sigma). Distinguish this from covariance effective rank based on sigma^2. Return effective rank unavailable when singular-value sum is numerically zero; disclose dtype and numerical tolerance. Check variance because tiny isotropic noise can produce high effective rank. For unit-normalized rows, compute mean off-diagonal cosine as (||sum(rows)||^2−N)/(N(N−1)); require at least two usable rows. The previous (cosine+1)/2 transformation is a directional-similarity index, not a calibrated collapse probability. Low rank alone establishes no HR@10 failure.

Keep one independently trained HSTU/checkpoint per category; no score fusion, additional fitted predictor or checkpoint reuse from other trials. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four category routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and the pinned evaluator. Bound probe inference and SVD work before execution because diagnostics consume the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. This diagnostic-only proposal leaves architecture, checkpoint format and the embedded predictor unchanged. Any subsequent architecture change must update the predictor writer and checkpoint loading together. Select training changes only by pinned macro validation HR@10. Do not inspect other trials; predictive validity across trials requires separately authorized records and remains exploratory under repeated validation tuning.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    existing = measure_existing_probes_with_explicit_missingness(train_loader)
    cases = fixed_training_cases(seed=42, cap_per_category=200)
    previous_mode = view.model.training
    try:
        view.model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            for case in cases:
                target = last_training_item(case)
                history = truncate_once(preceding_training_items(case), model_max_length)
                if len(history) < 3:
                    record_unavailable('insufficient_history'); continue
                candidates = fixed_unique_candidates(target, exclude=full_training_history(case), negatives=99)
                if candidates unavailable:
                    record_unavailable('insufficient_catalog'); continue
                n = len(history)
                k = min(5, (n-1)//2)
                variants = {
                    intact: history,
                    suffix: history[-min(10,n):],
                    remove_recent_context: history[:n-1-k] + history[-1:],
                    remove_old_context: history[k:],
                    remove_anchor: history[:-1]
                }
                for condition, retained_history in variants:
                    sequence = left_pad(retained_history)
                    features = view.log2feats(sequence)
                    final_index = greatest_nonzero_index(sequence)
                    scores = view.predict_score(features_at(features, final_index), candidates)
                    record_rank_hit_top10(scores, candidates, documented_tie_rule)
                    record_lengths_spans_anchor_and_repeat_target_status()
                if faithful_position_and_timestamp_preserving_masking_supported():
                    score_matched_context_masks_using_same_model_and_candidates()
                else:
                    record_unavailable('geometry_preserving_mask_not_supported')
                record_paired_changes_and_affected_flags()
            measure_bounded_representation_spectra_if_enabled()
    finally:
        view.model.train(previous_mode)
    aggregates = paired_user_bootstrap(replicates=2000, seed=42, within_category=True)
    macro_average_only_when_all_four_categories_have_eligible_users(aggregates)
    return {metrics: merge(existing, aggregates), metric_definitions: definitions_and_protocol}

optional_authorized_validation_probe(host_cases):
    require exact authorized users, targets and pinned candidates
    run the same paired inference conditions without modifying host evaluation
    report eligible-subset results separately from intact benchmark HR@10

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    embed measured metrics, definitions, sample counts, protocol and unavailable states
    distinguish in-sample training-prefix measurements from validation
    distinguish context effects, geometry effects and anchor changes
    prohibit interpreting sensitivity as causal intent or guaranteed generalization
    flag fixed-candidate scope, conditional uncertainty and repeated-selection limitations

originality.positive: Combines competitive target ranks with matched HSTU context interventions, explicit geometry controls and anchor-preserving comparisons.
originality.negative: Perturbation analysis, paired ranking comparisons and masking controls are established methods; the contribution is their careful adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Can guide focused experiments on recent-context weighting and reveal category-specific dependence without fitting additional predictors.
future_potential.negative: No evidence yet shows that these diagnostic effects predict validation gains; sensitivity can reflect memorization, geometry changes or fragility.

code_difficulty.positive: Compacted perturbations, competitive ranks and bounded representation SVD reuse existing inference interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful position-preserving attention masks may require internal HSTU integration; exact validation candidates, timestamp handling and paired aggregation need careful support.

related_work.title: [1] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU, including positional/temporal attention biases and multiplicative gating.
Provides architectural reasons why deletion can change attention geometry as well as item evidence.
limitations: Does not establish diagnostic thresholds or benefits of these perturbations on the four Amazon datasets.
Components described in the paper must not be assumed present in the supplied implementation.

related_work.title: [2] Disentangling User and Item Sequence Patterns
contributions: Examines sequence effects with shuffling controls that account for item availability.
limitations: Ordinary history perturbations can mix behavioral order with catalog effects.
Sensitivity does not identify causal user intent.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can change model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not replace the mandated pinned sampled-candidate selection metric.
Sampled HR@10 cannot establish full-catalog recommendation behavior.

related_work.title: [4] Sufficient Context
contributions: Studies context sufficiency alongside confidence for selective answering.
Motivates separating explicit metadata evidence from unknown compatibility.
limitations: Its question-answering findings motivate a diagnostic adaptation rather than establish recommendation improvement.
Missing specifications must not become negative preferences or ranking abstentions.

related_work.title: [5] The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality
contributions: Defines effective rank using entropy of normalized singular values.
limitations: Dimensionality alone does not establish recommendation quality.
Singular-value and covariance effective ranks differ; zero variance and negligible signal require explicit checks.

related_work.title: [6] Official HSTU implementation
contributions: Provides an implementation reference for HSTU attention, masking and relative bias mechanisms.
limitations: Reference code does not establish which mechanisms exist in the supplied corrected baseline.
A faithful diagnostic must preserve the actual implementation's position, timestamp and normalization conventions.

related_work.title: [7] RankMe: Assessing the Downstream Performance of Pretrained Self-Supervised Representations by Their Rank
contributions: Studies effective rank as a representation-quality proxy in self-supervised learning.
limitations: Transfer of its findings to HSTU recommendation remains a hypothesis.
Effective rank alone does not distinguish useful signal from tiny isotropic noise.

related_work.title: [8] Sequence or Pseudo-Sequence?
contributions: Reports limited sensitivity to history shuffling in studied recommendation settings and discusses timestamp ambiguity.
limitations: Its findings do not establish that order is irrelevant in these datasets or this HSTU implementation.

related_work.title: [9] Rank List Sensitivity
contributions: Studies changes in recommendations induced by small training-data perturbations.
limitations: Training-data perturbations differ from inference-history interventions.
Sensitivity alone establishes neither useful sequence dependence nor improved held-out accuracy.

related_work.title: [10] Inference at Scale
contributions: Provides supporting context for bootstrap and randomization approaches to uncertainty estimation.
limitations: Large-sample findings do not guarantee interval calibration for 200 users per category.
Conditional user bootstrap intervals exclude training-seed variability and repeated-selection bias.
